title: The effect of H1N1 vaccination on serum miRNA expression in children: A tale of caution for microRNA microarray studies.
ehr_evidence: Serum samples were obtained from children aged 6 months to 12 years enrolled in an open label randomised control trial of two pandemic influenza (H1N1) vaccines (clinical trial registration number: NCT00980850); miRNA expression was profiled from these biospecimens, not from electronic health records.
summary: In an open-label randomised controlled trial of two H1N1 influenza vaccines in 44 children aged 6 months to 12 years, Agilent microarray profiling of paired serum samples identified 19 differentially expressed miRNAs 21 days post-vaccination, but these were largely not validated by RT-qPCR and the one validated signal (miR-142-3p) was not replicated in an independent validation cohort.
key_findings: 19 miRNAs were differentially expressed post-vaccination (16 upregulated, 3 downregulated) with fold-change magnitude >1.2 after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment.
Most upregulated miRNA was miR-575 (fold-change = 1.57, adjusted p-value <0.001); most downregulated was miR-142-3p (fold-change = 0.77, adjusted p-value = 0.004).
RT-qPCR confirmed downregulation of miR-142-3p in the discovery cohort (mean fold-change = 0.805, log2 fold-change = -0.312, sd = 0.44, p = 0.003).
Downregulation of miR-30b was of borderline significance in the discovery cohort (p = 0.05).
miR-142-3p downregulation was not replicated in the independent validation cohort (mean fold-change = 1.1, log2 fold-change = 0.15, sd = 0.55, p = 0.89).
miR-30b-5p was not significantly differentially expressed in the validation cohort (mean fold-change = 1.11, log2 fold-change = 0.16, sd = 0.66, p = 0.86).
The majority of differentially expressed miRNAs could not be reliably detected/validated by RT-qPCR across both cohorts.
captured_features: Serum miRNA expression levels from Agilent miRNA microarray 60K (fluorescence values, log2 fold-change)
RT-qPCR Ct values and relative expression (2-ΔΔCt)
Vaccine group (AS03B adjuvanted split virion vs whole virion non-adjuvanted)
study_design: Open-label randomised controlled trial with a microarray discovery cohort (n=22) and an independent RT-qPCR validation cohort (n=22)
population: Children aged 6 months to 12 years enrolled in a UK multicentre H1N1 pandemic influenza vaccine trial
limitations: Only one microarray platform was used, limiting generalisation to other miRNA array technologies.
Many differentially expressed miRNAs could not be validated by RT-qPCR, with evidence of false-positive cross-hybridisation signals.
The validated miR-142-3p finding was not replicated in an independent validation cohort.
Only a single post-vaccination timepoint (3 weeks) was available, potentially missing early immune-response changes.
Low miRNA content in serum near the limit of detection and small sample sizes (22 per cohort).
data_availability_statement: Microarray expression data have been deposited into NCBI GEO (Series:GSE134227). RT-PCR data is included in the SupportingInformationfiles.
